assessment: This compelling study outlines how phylogenetic reconstruction can yield important insights into evolutionary aspects of assembly and function in acetylcholine receptors (AChRs). The authors elegantly demonstrate that ancestral AChR β subunits can form homomeric channels that share important functional hallmarks with their modern cousins, including unliganded gating. The work provides an intriguing framework to evaluate the evolution of the broader family of pentameric ligand-gated ion channels.
